record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: Is the following bulk-boundary correspondence for PEPS exactly true: the parent Hamiltonian of a projected entangled pair state is gapped if and only if the corresponding boundary states can be written as Gibbs states of one-dimensional short-range Hamiltonians whose interaction terms decay exponentially with distance?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a two-dimensional quantum lattice system on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with finite-dimensional local Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^d$ at each site. A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) is defined by placing, on each edge of the lattice, a maximally entangled pair in $\mathbb{C}^D \otimes \mathbb{C}^D$ (the auxiliary bond dimension is $D$), and at each vertex applying a linear map $A:(\mathbb{C}^D)^{\otimes 4}\to \mathbb{C}^d$. For any finite region $R\subset\mathbb{Z}^2$ this construction yields a state $|\psi_R\rangle$ on the physical sites in $R$ together with virtual (auxiliary) indices living on the bonds crossing the boundary $\partial R$. The "boundary state" associated with $R$ is the reduced density operator $\rho_{\partial R}$ obtained on the virtual boundary indices from the (suitably defined) PEPS transfer operator, viewed as a state on the Hilbert space $(\mathbb{C}^D)^{\otimes |\partial R|}$ of a one-dimensional ring.

A local "parent Hamiltonian" $H = \sum_{X} h_X$ associated with the PEPS is a translation-invariant frustration-free Hamiltonian with finite-range, bounded interaction terms $h_X\ge 0$ such that the PEPS is a ground state of $H$ in every finite volume. Such $H$ is called gapped if there exists $\gamma>0$, independent of the system size, such that in every finite volume the spectral gap above the ground space is at least $\gamma$.

A state $\rho_{\partial R}$ on a one-dimensional ring is called a Gibbs state of a short-range Hamiltonian with exponentially decaying interactions if $\rho_{\partial R} = e^{-K}/\mathrm{tr}(e^{-K})$ for some Hermitian operator $K = \sum_{Y\subset \partial R} K_Y$, where $\|K_Y\|\le C\, e^{-\alpha\,\mathrm{diam}(Y)}$ for some constants $C,\alpha>0$ independent of $R$.

Problem. Determine whether the following bulk–boundary correspondence holds exactly for PEPS: the parent Hamiltonian of the PEPS is gapped (uniformly in the system size) if and only if, for every sufficiently regular family of regions $R$, the corresponding boundary state $\rho_{\partial R}$ can be written as the Gibbs state of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian on $\partial R$ whose interaction terms decay exponentially with distance, with constants independent of $R$.
artifact.status_search_result: The "if" direction has been established in significant generality: Kastoryano, Lucia, and Pérez-García (Comm. Math. Phys. 2019, arXiv:1709.07691) proved that, for injective and MPO-injective PEPS, an approximate-factorization condition on boundary states of rectangular subregions—satisfied in particular by Gibbs states of local, finite-range one-dimensional Hamiltonians—implies a constant spectral gap of the bulk parent Hamiltonian in the thermodynamic limit. The full equivalence (in particular the converse direction, that a bulk gap forces the boundary state to be a Gibbs state of an exponentially-decaying short-range Hamiltonian) does not appear to be established in the literature, and the conjecture as a whole is still considered open.

status_evidence.title: Locality at the boundary implies gap in the bulk for 2D PEPS
status_evidence.snippet: An approximate factorization condition on the boundary state of rectangular subregions is sufficient to prove that the parent Hamiltonian of the bulk 2D PEPS has a constant gap in the thermodynamic limit; Gibbs states of local, finite-range Hamiltonians satisfy such conditions.
status_evidence.claim: The 'boundary locality ⇒ bulk gap' direction is rigorously established for injective and MPO-injective PEPS.

status_evidence.title: Locality at the Boundary Implies Gap in the Bulk for 2D PEPS
status_evidence.snippet: Provides one of the first rigorous connections between boundary theories and dynamical properties in an interacting many body system.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result toward the full bulk-boundary correspondence conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the bulk-boundary correspondence as a conjecture/question.
status_evidence.claim: The exact equivalence remains posed as an open conjecture.
